shorts.title: What you will learn: Virtual destructors
shorts.hook: Without virtual, half of your object is never cleaned.
shorts.script: Without virtual, half of your object is never cleaned. Today we fix a classic bug. It hides in code that looks right, and it leaks memory. When you delete an object through a base pointer, the compiler must find the right destructor. If the base destructor is not virtual, only the base destructor runs. The derived part is never cleaned. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Virtual destructors.

shorts.title: Virtual destructors in one minute
shorts.hook: When you delete an object through a base pointer
shorts.script: When you delete an object through a base pointer, the compiler must find the right destructor. If the base destructor is not virtual, only the base destructor runs. The derived part is never cleaned. The rule is simple. A class with any virtual function gets a virtual destructor. Think of a cleaning crew. If the manager only knows the lobby, the back room is never cleaned. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Virtual destructors in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: A smart pointer to Animal holds a Dog.
shorts.script: A smart pointer to Animal holds a Dog. The program prints working. At the end, the unique pointer deletes the object through the base type. Because the destructor is virtual, both Dog gone and Animal gone print. The rule is the same for smart pointers. The program prints working, then Dog gone, then Animal gone. Deleting through a base pointer needs a virtual destructor. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A base destructor that is not virtual
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in virtual destructors?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in virtual destructors? Bug of the Day. The class has a virtual function, but the destructor is not virtual. The compiler warns that deleting an object of polymorphic class type might cause undefined behaviour. Only the Animal part would be destroyed. Make the destructor virtual. Delete through a base pointer only runs the base destructor, when it is not virtual. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: A base destructor that is not virtual.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you check the rule in virtual destructors?
shorts.script: Can you check the rule in virtual destructors? Why was the destructor so tired? It had to clean up after the whole family. Write a base class with one virtual function. Add a virtual destructor. Explain in a comment why it is needed. Write your answer in the comments. Deleting through a base pointer needs a virtual destructor. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
